A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Latent Speech-Text Transformer work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, and equations, are readable and support matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original story-completion experiments, model-scaling results, patching ablations, embedding analyses, and three-run stability results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds LibriSpeech ASR/TTS results, synthesis-condition comparisons, lexical/syntactic scores, and alignment-noise testing.

M1.justification: The core architecture, next-token objective, and curriculum schedule remain unchanged. Table 6 adds a curriculum variant starting with silence-merged alignment patches, transitioning from average size 9.4 to 4; v1's reported curriculum used silence-separated patches. The expanded attention description documents existing components rather than establishing an architectural change.

E1.justification: v2 adds LibriSpeech ASR and TTS tasks, evaluates original SC/TSC speech alongside the retained resynthesized versions, and reports sWUGGY/sBLIMP evaluations that v1 explicitly omitted from its evaluation coverage. This substantially broadens coverage beyond narrative completion; the pre-training corpora remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds Curriculum (sil merged) as an internal comparator in the existing patching-strategy comparison. Base SpeechLLM and BPE SpeechLLM remain the external baselines in Tables 3–4; the new task evaluations otherwise reuse the baseline SpeechLLM.

E3.justification: New protocols include 1B-model fine-tuning on LibriSpeech clean, batch size 4 and sequence length 4096, ASR evaluation after 1k–4k iterations, and TTS evaluation after 20k iterations using Whisper-derived CER. Appendix A.11 introduces boundary perturbations of ±20–40 ms. Existing scaling experiments are relocated rather than newly introduced, while the NLL-gap evaluation is removed.

E4.justification: v2 adds synthesis-quality robustness comparisons in Appendix A.8, alignment-boundary noise testing in A.11, and the silence-merged curriculum ablation in Table 6. Conversely, v1's correct-versus-incorrect NLL separation analysis and Figure 7 disappear. The embedding, speech-proportion, BPE-alignment, and repeated-run analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The three-run means and standard deviations in Table 9 are unchanged, moving from v1 Appendix A.6 to v2 A.5. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and matched scaling scores remain unchanged. New Table 5 reports ASR WER of 6.8/10.4 for LST versus 140/202 for the baseline at 1k steps, and TTS CER of 14.1/16.2 versus 14.1/15.1 at 20k steps. Additional variant, synthesis-condition, lexical/syntactic, and alignment-noise findings are added; v1's NLL-gap results are removed.

T1.justification: The likelihood objective, patch definitions, and curriculum probability formula are unchanged. Appendix A.10 adds quantitative sequence/compute reasoning: token-mixture accounting and 4-to-1 speech patching yield 3.00-to-2.42 sequence units. Its claimed approximately 20% FLOPs reduction is not justified by the stated quadratic dependence. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion extend the central claims to faster, more stable ASR adaptation and reduced ASR/TTS inference cost without reconstruction-quality loss. These are substantive downstream claims beyond v1's demonstrated pre-training and story-completion contributions. The headline HellaSwag gains remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning preservation of phonetic detail, robustness to synthesis and alignment quality, and speech-data reuse making further scaling data-limited. It also develops an inference-efficiency explanation. Section 7 remains unchanged, however, leaving its exclusion of downstream adaptation inconsistent with the new experiments.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents pooled patch-query initialization and attention query/key/value roles, dataset licensing, downstream fine-tuning settings, and Whisper-based scoring. It replaces the future code-release pledge with a stated code link and reports release of resynthesized evaluation audio. Existing pre-training hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Radford et al. (2023) to support Whisper-based evaluation. The main related-work discussion and positioning relative to BLT, SpiritLM, and other speech-model efficiency approaches remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion are rewritten, and results are reorganized into controlled-budget, scaling, and downstream-analysis subsections. The appendices are substantially reorganized, separating model details from optimization and exchanging scaling material with the main text. Encoder/decoder terminology and publication headers also change.

P2.justification: v2 combines v1 Figures 5 and 6 into the two-panel Figure 4, removes the NLL-gap Figure 7, and moves the fixed-token scaling table into the appendix. It adds ASR/TTS, synthesis-condition, lexical/syntactic, and token-accounting tables, expands Table 6, and relocates the unchanged embedding visualization.

improvement.justification: The downstream and robustness experiments strengthen validation beyond v1's story-completion focus, while implementation details and reported code access improve reproducibility. These gains are qualified by removal of the NLL analysis, worse TTS 'other' CER despite the no-degradation claim, and Appendix A.10's inconsistent sequence-length/FLOPs reasoning. The stale limitation excluding downstream adaptation also weakens coherence, limiting the net improvement.
